The lift doors were closing when the manager, phone in hand, said, "Just change the sample count on that report, we're late." It was launch day, the floor was loud, and Deepika had no time to answer. She stepped out, went straight to her desk and wrote in her notebook: the date, the time, the exact words.

At lunch she opened the ethics policy on her laptop and read the section about requests like this. Then she found Divyansh, a senior on another team whom she trusted, and asked how these matters are usually handled. He told her whom to speak to and said her notes were a sensible start.

Nothing was settled yet, but her hands were steady when she went back to work.

qa.q: What did Deepika write in her notebook?
qa.a: The date, the time and the exact words.

qa.q: How was Deepika feeling by the time she went back to work?
qa.a: Deepika felt steadier and calmer, because her hands were steady once she had a record and knew where to turn.

qa.q: What could Deepika do if the manager repeated the request, and why?
qa.a: Deepika could decline politely and add the new request to her notes, because a dated record and the policy show she acted with care.

qa.q: How might Divyansh see being asked by Deepika?
qa.a: Divyansh may see trust and good sense, a colleague who checks the rules before acting, and want to guide her without taking over.

grounding: The employee writes down the date and words of the manager's request, reads the ethics policy and asks a trusted senior for guidance.

The request came on a Wednesday at 6:15 p.m., as the Bengaluru office was emptying. Ganga's manager stopped by and said, 'Update the site inspection report to say the fire exits were checked on the 2nd. They'll be checked next week anyway.'
Ganga said she'd look at it. The moment he left, she opened a note on her phone and typed exactly what he had said, with the date and time. Then she opened the company's code of conduct on the intranet and searched 'records'. Section 4 said employees must not create or alter documents to show events that didn't happen, and that concerns could be raised with a senior colleague or the ethics office.
The next morning she found Kamal, who had been in the safety team for eleven years, in the canteen. She showed him her note and the section.
Kamal read both and put his cup down. 'You did right to write it down. I'll come with you to the ethics office after lunch, and I'm asking facilities to check those exits today.'

qa.q: How might Ganga have felt when the manager walked away?
qa.a: Uneasy and alert, sure enough that it was wrong to start writing everything down at once.

qa.q: Why was writing down the exact words a wise first step?
qa.a: It gives a factual record of what was asked and when, which Kamal and the ethics office can act on.

qa.q: How does the request look to Kamal?
qa.a: Kamal, with years in safety, takes it seriously, backs Ganga's record, offers to go with her and gets the exits checked the same day.

grounding: Shows an employee writing down the date and words of a false-record request, reading the code of conduct and asking a trusted senior.

'Mahima di, do you have five minutes?' Neelam asked, hovering by the desk.
'For you, ten. What happened?'
Neelam put her phone on the desk. 'I wrote this last night. Word for word.'
Mahima read it aloud. '"Tuesday, 5:40 p.m. Sir said: mark all twelve new joiners as having attended the safety induction on Monday. We'll do the session later. Just sign as trainer."' She looked up. 'Did the session happen?'
'No. It's scheduled for next week.'
'Did you read the code of conduct?'
'Section six. False training records. It says to raise it with a senior or the compliance team.' Neelam swallowed. 'So I'm raising it with you. I don't want to get anyone in trouble. I just can't sign that.'
'You won't have to.' Mahima picked up her phone. 'I'm calling compliance now, and I'll ask them to move the induction to this week so the new joiners actually get it.'

qa.q: How many new joiners were to be marked as having attended?
What does Neelam swallowing before speaking suggest?
qa.a: She is nervous and a bit afraid of causing trouble, but determined not to sign a false record.
Bringing an exact written note and the policy section to a trusted senior, so the response could be quick and factual.

qa.q: How does Mahima see Neelam's concern?
qa.a: Mahima takes it seriously at once, calling compliance and making sure the new joiners actually get the safety training.

grounding: Shows an employee recording the exact words of a request to falsify training records, checking the code of conduct and raising it with a trusted senior.
